name: plant_case_template
provenance: REPLACE: who measured what, where and when (coil ids, dates, instruments).
notes: TEMPLATE for a real problem: replace every mill, pass and material value with your own (SI units: m, Pa, kg, N/m, m/s, Hz, rad). The values shown are the synthetic demo mill, not your mill. Leave an observation null when you have not looked: null means 'not observed' and never counts against a hypothesis.

schedule (optional): add your pass schedule as a list of {label, entry_thickness_m, exit_thickness_m, mean_flow_stress_pa, friction_coefficient, entry_tension_pa, exit_tension_pa, exit_speed_m_s} to get the per-pass chatter margin and ripple table.

observation.orientation: how the marks run across the strip: 'transverse' (straight across), 'diagonal', 'chevron' (herringbone V shapes), 'longitudinal' (lengthwise bands along the rolling direction), 'irregular', or null.

observation.pitch_observations: MOST VALUABLE. Stone or etch a strip sample and measure the distance between successive marks along the rolling direction (pitch_m), together with the steady exit speed the sample was rolled at (exit_speed_m_s). Do it at two clearly different speeds (at least 20 % apart): if the pitch grows in proportion to speed the source is a fixed-frequency vibration (chatter, resonance); if the pitch stays the same the source is locked to a roll, bearing, gear or coil.
observation.faces: 'both' if the marks are visible on top and bottom strip faces, 'one' if only on one face.

observation.gauge_variation_detected: true if the exit thickness gauge / X-ray shows a periodic thickness variation at the mark frequency, false if the gauge is clean at that frequency; gauge_variation_amplitude_m: its peak-to-peak size in metres if known (recorded only).

observation.first_seen: 'bite_exit' if the marks appear straight out of the roll bite, 'incoming_strip' if the entry coil already has them, 'after_bending_or_levelling' if they appear only after a deflector roll, coiler or leveller.
observation.disappears_after_work_roll_change / disappears_after_backup_roll_change: true/false from a roll-change test, null if not tried.
observation.onset_above_exit_speed_m_s: the exit speed above which the marks start, if there is such a threshold.
observation.worse_at_thinner_gauge: true if the marks are more frequent or stronger at thinner exit gauge.

observation.band_positions_across_width_m: for lengthwise bands only: band positions measured on the same barrel coordinate as the coolant header (0 at the header start), after removing strip tracking offset.
observation.measured_vibration_hz: dominant stand vibration frequency from a chock accelerometer at the operating speed, if measured.

kinematics: list work-roll and backup-roll bearings (rolling elements, element and pitch diameters, contact angle), gear meshes (teeth and shaft speed ratio to the work roll) and known grinder-mark counts; without them the drive/bearing hypothesis cannot be checked.
coolant: header geometry and any blocked nozzles; lubrication: base-oil viscosity, pressure-viscosity coefficient and roll/strip roughness. Set either to null if unknown.

model_options.bite_response_override: for gauges where the slab model rejects (thin hard strip, foil; see docs/band-diagnosis.md), supply bite force and sensitivities from a plant or foil mill model here instead of null.

case_schema physicroll.band_case.v2: every v1 key stays; the six sections below are optional (null = not supplied, the result section then says NOT_SUPPLIED). Values shown are the synthetic demo mill, not your mill.

width_model (lengthwise bands): work-roll thermal and strip-shape model. roll = work-roll steel properties and barrel length; spray_header = nozzle pitch, standoff, fan angle, offset angle, mean spray heat-transfer coefficient and background coefficient; coolant_temperature_k; blocked_nozzle_indices (0 = first nozzle from the header start) or nozzle_levels (one flow level 0..1 per nozzle); events = valve switching or intermittent blockage [{start_s, duration_s, nozzle_indices, level}]; rolls_carrying_stripe = 1 if one header is affected, 2 if both; roll_heat_fraction_per_roll and bite_heat_per_width_w_m may stay null (computed; a null roll_heat_fraction_per_roll is derived from tribology.strip_heat_fraction as (1 - strip share)/2, and if both are given and disagree the result flags HEAT_PARTITION_INPUTS_INCONSISTENT: the roll thermal model uses the width-model value, pass heating the tribology value); crowns, heredity coefficient, incoming ridges, coil, previous widths, grinding, cooling-zone pitch, deflector radius and lateral compressive stress are optional and switch on the corresponding screens.

tribology: rolling-oil viscosity law, roll/strip roughness and temperatures. The friction closure is a PLACEHOLDER (not fitted): the computed friction is shown beside your value; it replaces it only with use_computed_friction true. Its slope with speed is the useful output (speed-consistent chatter critical speed).

hardening: 'power' {yield_stress_pa, strength_coefficient_pa, exponent} or 'voce' {initial_stress_pa, saturation_stress_pa, characteristic_strain, stage_iv_slope_pa} with provenance, prior_equivalent_strain and the reference (annealed) thickness; with use_computed_flow_stress true the computed flow stress replaces the supplied one on every pass.

gauge_control: gaugemeter AGC compensation gain (0..1), cylinder bandwidth and optional force filter; drive: drive-train inertias and shaft stiffnesses (torsional modes); incoming_variation: relative hardness variation of the incoming coil and whether it repeats once per decoiler revolution.
observation.lengthwise_continuity: 'continuous' if a band runs along the whole coil, 'intermittent' if bands appear only for a while, 'both' if you see both kinds.
observation.intermittent_duration_s: typical time a short-lived band lasts (seconds of rolling).
observation.band_width_m / band_spacing_m: typical width of one band across the strip, and the distance between neighbouring bands if they are roughly regular.
observation.band_positions_across_width_m (lengthwise bands): measure on the barrel coordinate of the coolant header (0 at the header start), as for v1.

observation.positions_repeat_across_coils: true if the bands sit at the same width positions on successive coils; positions_change_after_work_roll_change: true if they move (or vanish) after a work-roll change.
observation.changes_with_coolant_zone_switching: true if the bands come and go when coolant zones (flatness control valves) switch.

observation.appearance: 'gloss_or_shade' (bright/dull stripe), 'loose_or_buckle' (wavy, loose band), 'tight' (tight stripe), 'stain' (oil/coolant stain, often after annealing), 'crease_or_flute' (sharp fold or flute).
observation.visible_only_after_tension_release: true if the bands are invisible in the mill and show only on the coil or after slitting (latent tension stripes).
observation.worse_toward_outer_wraps: true if the band is stronger toward the outside of the wound coil; changes_with_tension: true if changing the strip tension changes the bands.

observation.follows_previous_strip_edges: true if band edges line up with the edges of narrower strip rolled earlier on the same work rolls; worse_at_higher_speed: true if the bands get worse as the mill speeds up.

Battery foil (exit gauge below 100 um): the result then carries a foil_regime block and the flag CLOSED_GAP_ROLLING_LIKELY_ROLL_KISSING_NOT_MODELLED: the mill is in or near closed-gap rolling, which the tool does not model; the lever table and the gauge-control section assume an open gap.

observation.worse_at_lower_tension: true if the bands are more visible when the strip tension is lower and fade above some tension (step the exit tension and note at which tension they fade). Note: a band hidden under mill tension (a latent thermal stripe) is also worse at lower tension.

observation.changes_with_ironing_roll_pressure: true if the bands change when the ironing-roll pressure (per side) is changed; changes_with_exit_air_blowoff: true if they change when the exit air blow-off is reduced or redirected.
observation.changes_after_roll_wiper_cleaning: true if the bands change or go after the roll wipers are cleaned (wiper debris), false if they stay.
observation.tracks_speed_changes: true if the bands appear, move or fade when the mill speed changes, false if they ignore speed changes.
observation.appeared_after_narrower_coil: true if the bands started when a wider coil was rolled after a narrower one (without a backup-roll change).

width_model.shape_inputs (optional, null = derive from the bite): when no bite model solves the pass (foil), supply {strip_stiffness_per_width_pa, exit_tension_force_sensitivity_per_width_m, bite_half_length_m, provenance} from a plant foil model; they then drive the strip-shape chain (transfer, flatness, onset heights) of the case pass and take precedence over a derived bite. Without a bite and without them the shape parts are not assessable and the rest of the width section still runs; the roll thermal stripes then need bite_heat_per_width_w_m supplied.

material.final_pass_doubled (optional, v2): whether the thinnest pass of the case (schedule rows and the case pass) is rolled doubled, two sheets in one bite. null = not stated (the foil-regime block then asks the plant); false = single-sheet stated (the block records it and notes that both faces are roll-side, so observation.faces is worth recording); true = doubled stated (flag DOUBLED_FINAL_PASS_NOT_MODELLED: the tool models one sheet in the bite). It has no effect when the case is not in the foil regime (exit gauge of 100 um or more, no foil_regime block).

material.product (optional, v2): a product id from the thin-gauge catalogue (physicroll/band_products.py, docs/thin-gauge-products.md): battery_collector_foil, battery_pouch_laminate_foil, capacitor_anode_foil_high_voltage, capacitor_anode_foil_low_voltage, capacitor_cathode_foil, pharma_blister_lidding, pharma_cold_form_foil, pharma_strip_pack_foil, household_foil, household_foil_heavy_duty, converter_foil, cigarette_liner_foil, dairy_lidding_foil, container_foil_wrinkle_wall, container_foil_smooth_wall, container_foil_retortable, brazed_fin_stock, brazing_sheet_tube, hvac_fin_stock, litho_sheet, can_body_stock, can_end_stock, closure_sheet, transformer_strip. With it the result carries a product_check: every pass against the published envelope of that product (final gauge, per-pass and final-pass reduction, final-pass entry gauge, speed, rolled mode, alloy, temper, flow stress as an indicator) and the nearest published passes. It is a literature check and never changes the hypothesis scores; an unknown id is rejected with the list of valid ids. material.alloy may carry a prefix (AA1235, EN AW-1235): the check uses the bare designation.

width_model.spray_wetted_arc_rad (optional, null = not given): the arc of the roll circumference [rad, in (0, 2*pi]] that the coolant spray wets. The model's spray_mean_htc_w_m2k is a mean around the roll; with the arc, thermal_check also shows the equivalent coefficient inside the jet zone, h_bg + spray_mean_htc * 2*pi/arc. It does not enter the roll thermal model.

tribology.oil_flash_point_k and tribology.oil_supply_temperature_cap_k (optional, null = not given, 250-700 K): the flash point of your rolling oil (data sheet) and a site or insurer cap on the oil supply temperature. thermal_check.fire_limits compares the oil temperatures and the modelled strip exit temperatures with them (a rule check; a modelled exit temperature is not a coil temperature); there is no default limit.

measurement (optional, v2; null = not supplied): {"shapemeter": {zone_width_m, zone_count, edge_zone_width_m, edge_zone_count_per_side, centre_m, neighbour_spreading_fraction, resolution_i_units, provenance}, "thickness_gauge": null}. The shapemeter block gives what each zone of a flatness roll with that zone width would read for every modelled band (zone means of the model profile; no flatness controller is modelled). Zone width, count and edge zones come from the shapemeter data sheet or the level-2 configuration; leave neighbour_spreading_fraction at 0 unless the vendor states it, and resolution_i_units null unless the vendor gives one.

width_model.strip_temperature (optional, null = not supplied): a measured or assumed strip temperature scan across the width, {positions_m (>= 3, increasing, on the barrel), temperature_k (one per position, 250-700 K), expansion_coefficient_per_k (null = 23.6e-6 /K, a textbook value), provenance}. It is not computed by the tool. The result then shows flatness as a shapemeter measures it hot (model flatness plus about 2.4 I-units per kelvin) beside the flatness after the coil has cooled.

width_model.friction_stripe_screen (optional, null = not supplied): {reference_half_peak_width_m (null = 0.1 m), stripes: [{position_m, half_peak_width_m, friction_change_fraction (relative change of the pass friction, -0.9 to 5, not 0), label}]}. A screening estimate of a local friction or oil-film difference across the width as a band source: I-units per 1 % friction per pass (with and without the exit-tension feedback) and the flatness of each supplied stripe; the list may be empty. It never changes a score.

width_model.roll_ground_profile (optional, null = not supplied): a measured roll profile from a grinder report, {positions_m (>= 5, increasing, on the barrel, from the barrel end where the spray header starts), radius_deviation_m (RADIUS, half a diameter deviation, positive = larger roll, one per position), detrend_order (default 2: the crown is removed; null = none), rolls_carrying (1 or 2), provenance}. It goes through the same transfer as a thermal stripe; it never changes a score.
